changes: Typed workers serialize node proofs directly into the final result packet, using one fallibly allocated buffer capped at the proof limit plus the fixed result header. Native node values are released before packet completion.

The coordinator consumes and compacts an admitted response buffer in place, retaining its original bounded capacity through proof use. It allocates no second proof byte buffer; metadata and validation allocations remain separately bounded.
Exact assignment/request binding compares every decoded canonical field, dependency and original proof byte instead of re-encoding the complete request.

Typed dispatch sends the token-length prefix, token and retained request as separate slices under the same frame header. It checks the combined bound before any write and retains existing pending/poisoned state on transport errors.

Both wire families match the frozen serializer reference. Pointer/capacity, oversized storage, malformed requests/results, truncation, control-field substitution and multipart framing checks pass in both lane configurations.
Two full-size finalizers preserve the archived registry and every arithmetic-stage operation count while exercising direct serialization and coordinator buffer reuse.
limitations: Protocol limits describe backing-vector capacity, not complete physical RSS or scheduler phases. Node proof containers, verifier scratch, allocator/driver overhead and complete cache/callback overlaps still require enclosing lifetime reservations.

Coordinator compaction copies bytes within the same buffer. Compatibility APIs that accept borrowed serialized proofs or responses still allocate bounded owned output buffers; this is not a universal zero-copy claim.
The retained frame capacity remains charged to the returned proof, including unused header/storage space. Limits must use capacity rather than serialized length.

Other bounded storage scopes retain their previous limits. No scheduler allowance was reduced from observed peaks. Ordinary pool admission rejects this qualification profile without complete lifetime phases.

The 3 GiB worker, 4 GiB aggregate host, 7 GiB managed GPU and 1 GiB allocation caps remain enforced. These isolated finalizer timings do not establish sustained transaction throughput or a performance gain.
Broader transaction workloads, nonempty-child full-size merges, larger blocks, sustained pool throughput, multiple GPUs and AMD/Metal qualification remain open.
